Point-to-point. This method compares the index level at two points in time, such as the beginning and ending dates of the time period.

Averaging. This method compares an average of the index levels at periodic intervals during the time period to the index level at the beginning of the time period.
answer: Indexed annuities can use different methods to measure index changes over a time period. With a point-to-point method, the contract compares the index level at two dates, such as the period’s beginning and end. With an averaging method, it compares the index level at the beginning with an average of index levels measured at intervals during the period. The methods differ in which index values are used for the comparison; check the contract to see which method it uses.
